why: Every protocol, version, kind and payload member set this stack declares, with who produces each kind and who reads it. The `protocol-inventory` gate compares this file against the live registries in both directions, because a prose inventory in a document is not checked by anything: docs/context.md claimed 36 files, 140 tests and 9 gates at the commit where the truth was 44, 177 and 11, and nothing noticed. The member lists are compared with the value each kind declares once (`KindRule.members`, through `defineKind`), which is the same value the parse boundary applies to the payload before the parser runs — so this file can only disagree with the code when one of the two was edited, which is what makes adding a member a recorded act rather than a drift. Rounds three to five inferred the member set by handing each parser payloads and reading the refusal, and round five showed that mechanism's own limit: a parser that closes its payload over a member it never names is reached by no sample of a family that grows only by named members. Nothing is sampled now, and a kind whose row is a bare name is refused, as is a row that lists a member the declaration does not name. `producedBy` and `readBy` are not machine-checkable; they are here so that adding a shape is a recorded act with a named consumer, which is the one thing the previous system never had to do. What this file does not record: the closed shapes inside a payload (`nested`), which the kinds declare and the ledger's comparison does not reach.

protocols.subject: the agent id
protocols.producedBy: scripts/*.mjs deployments (a deployment opens the node before recording it)

protocols.subject: the environment id
protocols.producedBy: src/environment/protocol.ts revision/created (a deployment mints revisions) and src/release/commands.ts publish (the one conditional update)
protocols.readBy: src/environment/binding.ts assertPinnedRevision, src/task/commands.ts (the pin gate), src/release/commands.ts (the head it expects)

protocols.subject: the evaluation id
protocols.producedBy: src/measure/commands.ts createMeasureCommands; the three verification kinds are emitted by the implementation the frozen plan names, by content digest
protocols.readBy: src/measure/view.ts projectEvaluation (the aggregate, the missing denominator and the admissibility of one candidate) and caliberDigestOf (the comparability a round pools on)

protocols.subject: the environment whose head is moving
protocols.producedBy: src/release/commands.ts createReleaseCommands (draft, and approve behind the native approval seam)
protocols.readBy: src/release/commands.ts publish (a head may only move to an approved revision)

protocols.subject: the round id
protocols.producedBy: src/strategy/commands.ts createStrategyCommands (the submission gate is a precondition of candidate/submitted; the annealed budget is derived, never supplied)
protocols.readBy: src/strategy/view.ts projectRound (each slot's aggregate, frozen gain and admissibility, then the selection, reading the direction from measure's evaluation/opened.metric.direction), src/strategy/plan.ts (the round's frozen plan)

protocols.subject: the task id
protocols.producedBy: src/task/commands.ts createTaskCommands (the only surface that produces task facts)
protocols.readBy: src/task/view.ts projectTask/projectReceipt, src/task/tree.ts projectTree, src/task/consumption.ts unconsumedMethods
